ai.literal: Glory to a person is inner wealth; disgrace to a person is saying 'we shall live having lost that'.
ai.translation: True glory for a person is their inner wealth of spirit. Disgrace is thinking, 'We can live even after losing it.'
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்கு உண்மையான பெருமை என்பது அவரது உள்ளத்தில் இருக்கும் ஊக்கமே ஆகும். அந்த ஊக்கத்தை இழந்துவிட்டும் நாம் வாழ்வோம் என்று நினைப்பது அவருக்கு இழிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes true glory and what constitutes disgrace for an individual. The word 'ஒளி' (light) metaphorically stands for glory or brilliance, which the poet identifies as 'உள்ள வெறுக்கை', the inner wealth of spirit or motivation. Conversely, 'இளி' means disgrace or shame. The greatest shame is not poverty or failure, but the very thought that one can continue to live after losing that inner wealth. The contrast between inner abundance and the mere physical continuation of life highlights the importance of spirit in achieving greatness.

ai.literal: Birth is alike to all lives; greatness is not alike, by the difference of doing deeds.
ai.translation: Birth is the same for all living beings, but their greatness is not equal, due to the differences in the deeds they do.
ai.modern: பிறப்பால் எல்லா உயிர்களும் சமமே. ஆனால் அவர்கள் செய்யும் செயல்களின் வேறுபாட்டால் அவர்களின் சிறப்புகள் சமமாக இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes a fundamental equality among all living beings at the moment of birth. The word 'piṟappu' (birth) is paired with 'okkum' (is alike), stating that no one is born inherently superior. However, 'ciṟappu' (greatness or distinction) does not remain equal ('ovvā'). This distinction arises solely through 'cey toḻil vēṟṟumaiyān', meaning the differences in the actions or work that individuals choose to do. Thus, true greatness is earned through one's deeds, not inherited by birth.

ai.literal: High even if being, high those who are not, high they are not; low even if being, low those who are not, low they are not.
ai.translation: Even if placed in a high position, those who lack greatness are not truly high. Even if placed in a low position, those who do not lack greatness are not truly low.
ai.modern: உயர்ந்த நிலையில் இருந்தாலும், பெருமை இல்லாதவர்கள் உயர்ந்தவர்கள் ஆக மாட்டார்கள். தாழ்ந்த நிலையில் இருந்தாலும், சிறுமை இல்லாதவர்கள் தாழ்ந்தவர்கள் ஆக மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true greatness by separating it from mere social or material status. The words 'mēl' (high) and 'kīḻ' (low) are used in two senses: first to denote outward position, and second to denote inner character. Even if placed in a high position, people without noble qualities are not truly high. Conversely, people with noble qualities remain high in character even if they are placed in a low position.

ai.literal: Like women of singleness indeed, greatness too exists if oneself having guarded oneself conducts oneself.
ai.translation: Just like women of single-minded devotion, true greatness exists only if one guards oneself and behaves with discipline.
ai.modern: கற்புடைய பெண்களைப் போல, ஒருவன் தன்னைத் தானே காத்துக்கொண்டு நல்வழியில் நடந்தால் மட்டுமே அவனுக்குப் பெருமை நிலைத்திருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the preservation of greatness to the single-minded devotion of chaste women. The word 'ஒருமை' (singleness) here refers to unwavering moral focus or chastity. Just as such women protect their own virtue, a person must actively guard their own character to maintain their greatness. Greatness is not a permanent given; it exists only as long as one conducts oneself with disciplined self-restraint.

ai.literal: Greatness those-who-possess will-perform in-the-proper-way rarity possessing deed.
ai.translation: Those who possess greatness will perform difficult deeds in the proper way.
ai.modern: பெருமை குணம் கொண்டவர்கள், மற்றவர்களால் செய்வதற்கு அரிய செயல்களை உரிய வழியில் செய்து முடிப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the nature of great people through their actions. While ordinary people might avoid difficult tasks, those with greatness take on rare and challenging deeds. Furthermore, they do not just attempt them, but successfully complete them in the proper way. The word 'ஆற்றின்' emphasizes that they follow the right method to achieve these extraordinary results.

ai.literal: Small people's mind-in is not, great people having cherished we will keep saying intention.
ai.translation: The intention to cherish and keep the company of the great does not exist in the minds of the small.
ai.modern: பெரியவர்களைப் போற்றிப் பாதுகாப்போம் என்ற எண்ணம் சிறியவர்களின் மனதில் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the mindset of the small-minded with the respect owed to the great. The phrase 'பேணிக் கொள்வேம்' means to cherish and keep close. The word 'நோக்கு' here means intention or perspective, rather than just a physical look. The text states that such an intention simply does not exist within the consciousness ('உணர்ச்சியுள்') of petty individuals.

ai.literal: Transgression indeed doing deed-natured will become even greatness itself excellence with those who lack if it falls.
ai.translation: Even high status, if it falls to those who lack true excellence, will result only in deeds of arrogant transgression.
ai.modern: சீர்மை இல்லாதவர்களிடம் சிறப்பு சேர்ந்தால், அது வரம்பு மீறிய செயல்களைச் செய்யும் தன்மையுடையதாகவே மாறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains what happens when unworthy people attain power or wealth. The word 'சிறப்பு' refers to high status or prosperity, while 'சீர்' means true inner excellence. If greatness falls to those without such excellence, they will not use it well; instead, their actions will be characterized by 'இறப்பு', meaning transgression or crossing moral limits.

ai.literal: Will be humble indeed always greatness; smallness will adorn indeed oneself having admired.
ai.translation: Greatness will always be humble. Smallness will adorn itself with self-admiration.
ai.modern: பெருமைக்குரியவர்கள் எப்போதும் பணிவாகவே இருப்பார்கள். ஆனால் சிறுமைக்குணம் கொண்டவர்கள் தங்களை நாமே வியந்து புகழ்ந்து கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts true greatness with smallness of character. The word 'பெருமை' (greatness) is paired with 'பணியும்' (will bow), showing that great people naturally and always exhibit humility. In contrast, 'சிறுமை' (smallness) is described as 'தன்னை வியந்து அணியும்'—admiring oneself and wearing that self-praise as an adornment. The suffix 'ஆம்' attached to both verbs emphasizes that these are the inherent, unchanging habits of such natures.

ai.literal: Greatness [is] pride absence; smallness [is] pride having ridden completely.
ai.translation: Greatness is the absence of pride. Smallness is being completely carried away by pride.
ai.modern: பெருமை என்பது தற்பெருமை இல்லாமல் இருப்பதாகும். சிறுமை என்பது தற்பெருமையின் மீது ஏறிச் சவாரி செய்வதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts true greatness with smallness of character by looking at how they relate to pride. Greatness is defined simply as the complete absence of arrogance. Smallness, on the other hand, is depicted with the striking image of riding on pride, meaning the person is entirely driven and carried away by conceit. The word 'ஊர்ந்து' (riding or mounting) vividly shows how petty individuals let arrogance control their behavior.

ai.literal: Flaw will-hide greatness, meanness indeed fault-only having-spoken will-leave.
ai.translation: Greatness hides the flaws of others, but meanness will speak only of their faults.
ai.modern: பெருமைக்குரியவர்கள் மற்றவர்களின் குறைகளை மறைப்பார்கள். ஆனால் சிறுமைக்குணம் கொண்டவர்கள் மற்றவர்களின் குற்றங்களையே கூறிக்கொண்டிருப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the behavior of the great and the mean-spirited towards others. The word 'aṟṟam' can mean an end or a secret, but here it specifically refers to a vulnerability or a flaw that should be kept private. True greatness chooses to cover and protect the weaknesses of others. In contrast, meanness actively seeks out and broadcasts only the faults of others, as emphasized by the exclusive particle 'ē' in 'kuṟṟamē'.
